description: Resolve a public IP or dotted hostname to country, region, city, coordinates, ASN, organization, timezone, and proxy/hosting/mobile flags. Supply target for one lookup or targets for an ordered batch, never both; blank target and empty targets are unset. Batches process the first 100 positions (duplicates retained) and disclose every remainder in unprocessedTargets; at most 1000 inputs are accepted. Each batch position reports its result or an error with recovery, so cached and local outcomes survive quota refusals. The provider is called directly, never the target. Hostnames are DNS-resolved and resolvedIp names the located address. Private/reserved addresses have no public geolocation. Results are best-effort, city-level at best; VPNs, proxies, mobile NAT, and anycast defeat IP-to-location. Read proxy, hosting, and mobile before trusting coordinates: true describes infrastructure, not the user. Absent metadata remains unknown. source names the provider. Single and batch quotas are independent; cache hits consume neither quota.

target.description: One public IP or dotted hostname; mutually exclusive with nonempty targets.

targets.description: Ordered public IPs or dotted hostnames; first 100 positions are served, every remainder is disclosed. Mutually exclusive with nonblank target.

items.description: A public IPv4/IPv6 address or a hostname (e.g. "8.8.8.8" or "example.com").

name: toolkit_geolocate_ip

asn.description: Autonomous System number, e.g. "AS15169". Absent on providers that omit it.

country.description: Country name. Absent when the provider does not report it.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Absent when unknown.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `rate_limited`: The endpoint request quota or provider cooldown is exhausted. `unresolvable_host`: A hostname target failed DNS resolution. `private_target`: The target resolves to a private/reserved IP with no public geolocation. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

hosting.description: True when the address belongs to a hosting or datacenter network, so the location is a facility rather than a person. Absent when unreported.

latitude.description: Latitude in decimal degrees. Absent when unknown.

longitude.description: Longitude in decimal degrees. Absent when unknown.

mobile.description: True when the address belongs to a mobile carrier network, where NAT can place the location far from the device. Absent when unreported.

org.description: Owning organization or ISP, e.g. "Google LLC". Absent when unknown.

proxy.description: True when the address is a known proxy, VPN, or Tor exit — the location describes the exit node, not the user. Absent when the provider does not report it.

region.description: Region or state name. Absent when unknown.

resolvedIp.description: The IP that was actually located (a supplied hostname is resolved to this first).

results.description: Ordered results or failures for the first 100 input positions.
